page: Microsoft Azure D2s_v6 is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz across 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core via hyper-threading. The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an extensive cache hierarchy with 260 MB of L3 cache, as well as support for Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512 vector instruction sets. The instance includes no local ephemeral storage and features no dedicated GPUs, requiring external remote block volumes for persistent disk storage.

Benchmark results show balanced single-core execution alongside constrained multi-core throughput due to its single physical core constraint. Single-threaded tasks demonstrate competitive performance, evidenced by strong gzip compression throughput of 31.33 GB/sec and average single-core scores in both Geekbench (1709.0) and stress-ng (1940.78). In contrast, multi-threaded workloads are limited, with stress-ng multi-core registering in the bottom 10% and Geekbench multi-core reaching 2104.0. Large-block uncached memory bandwidth is also limited, achieving 20.8 GB/sec for reads and 14.3 GB/sec for writes. Redis operations measure 2.95 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 4.4 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2s_v6 provides an accessible entry point to modern Intel Xeon compute capabilities for workloads that do not demand extensive parallel throughput or local NVMe scratch space. The trade-off centers on scaling limitations: workloads requiring wide multi-threading, high uncached memory bandwidth, or intensive database operations may experience resource contention on the single physical core. Consequently, this server is well matched for lightweight web servers, development environments, background job workers, microservices, and modest CI/CD build tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D2s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 2 dedicated vCPUs spanning a single physical hyper-threaded core and 8.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing remote storage volumes for disk operations. Supported CPU instruction sets include AVX-512 and AMX matrix extensions. Single-core performance is solid, highlighted by strong gzip compression at 31.33 GB/sec and average Geekbench single-core scores. However, multi-core throughput and uncached memory bandwidth show clear limitations inherent to its dual-vCPU single-core footprint. Delivering a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, the D2s_v6 functions efficiently for lightweight microservices, testing environments, web serving, and small background utilities.
